log: -: You heave. They heave. The door stays shut. Four of them is more than one of you.
-: Pete comes down the stairs last. He looks at you, straining at the door. He looks at the crew, straining at you.
-: He tries one more time. You can see him decide to.
pete: Captain. There's nobody in there. It's the old cloud. From the first night. It's been in there all along. That's what's growling.
captain: It's BROGATH.
pete: ...
-: He gives up. You see that too. He changes his face. He goes very serious.
pete: ...Yes. You're right, Captain. Brogath is trapped in there.
pete: And as long as this door stays SHUT, he can't get out. And he can't blast the treasure away. The door is what's keeping him in. You see?
-: You stop pulling.
captain: ...The door keeps him in.
pete: The door keeps him in.
captain: Then... nobody opens the door.
pete: Nobody opens the door. EVER.
-: Everybody lets go of you, very slowly. You stand back from the door. You straighten your coat. It's working. It's actually working.
-: Then you frown.
captain: ...Which Brogath?
pete: What?
captain: There's one in there. And there's one on deck, cardboard. And there's YOU. Which Brogath is in the treasure room, Pete?
-: Pete opens his mouth. Pete closes it. Pete looks at Gristle. Gristle shakes his head, slowly. It's multiplying.
-: Back on deck. The storm going round. You march straight to the helm, where Pete (where BROGATH) was leaning.
captain: Brogath.
pete: Pete.
captain: You laid hands on my helm. That's a challenge for command. I accept. We settle it the way captains settle it.
pete: How's that?
captain: NAVIGATION. Keep her steady through the storm. Whoever holds the best course is captain.
pete: Captain. Steering's literally already your job. You're the captain. Nobody's challenging anything. I just LEANED.
captain: Then you won't mind watching me do it, will you, Brogath.
-: A gust takes her. She swings off.
pete: (behind you, to Gristle) He's good at this.
captain: (not turning round) Brogath is taking NOTES.
-: Tok. A token comes down on the binnacle, and another on the deck.
captain: It's CAMPAIGNING.
-: Another gust, from the other side.
captain: ...I'd vote for that.
jim: You'd vote for 'no fun'?
captain: I'd vote for no BROGATHS.
-: The biggest yet. The whole ship heels.
bob: A DEBATE? On the television?
pete: There's no election. There's never been an election. You don't ELECT a captain at sea in a storm.
squawks: Do now.
-: And from below, one more time, the treasure-room growl. Long, low, old, through every plank of the ship.
-: GRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR.
captain: THE THIRD BROGATH.
garrick: (coming up the ladder, quietly, hands up) Captain. Captain, listen to me. That one's not Brogath.

garrick: That growl is mine. From the treasure room. The very first night. That's MY old fart, Captain. It's been in there ever since. It's been growling down there for a month. It's... it's a sort of a pet now.
-: Silence on deck.
-: You look at him. Garrick. Just Garrick, in a burgundy suit, with flat hair, telling you the truth.
-: For one moment, the purple goes out of the edges of things. The deck is the deck. The storm is the storm. Garrick is Garrick.
captain: ...Your old fart.
garrick: My old fart.
captain: ...In the treasure room. Not Brogath.
garrick: Not Brogath.
captain: ...Right. Right. That makes sense. That makes SENSE.
-: Everybody breathes out. Pete actually sits down on the deck.
captain: (nodding slowly) Your old fart. In the treasure room.
captain: But Pete is still Brogath.
pete: (from the deck, to the sky) WHY DO WE KEEP LOSING PROGRESS?
-: Tok. One more token lands at his feet. He doesn't pick it up. Squawks does.
squawks: Tonight.
